sentences.text: This appeal by the Insurance Company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 27.03.2023 passed by First Additional Member, M.A.C.T., Dewas (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.196/2020 on account of exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability on the ground of false implication of offending vehicle.

2. The brief facts of the case is that on 26.02.2020, at 05:00 PM, pillion rider of motorcycle bearing Registration No. MP41 MH 0741, Bheru Singh was going from Dewas to Village Tumdavada along with his nephew Shekhar Patel.

As soon as he reached Tumdavada village, Driver of offending vehicle car bearing Registration No.MP43 CA 9994 driving in rash and negligent manner dashed the motorcycle, due to which, the applicant suffered injuries on his hands, legs, waist, head and fracture of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35276 2 MA-2838-2023 tibia and fibula bone on his left leg.
3. The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal as well as seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.19,75,000/-.

4. Driver and owner of offending vehicle as well as Insurance Company filed their written Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Bherusingh Kalota on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145052022/
1 statements and denied all the averments.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The owner of the offending vehicle denied the accident and stated in written statement that he was in possession of the offending vehicle at the time of accident and there was no accident occurred by the offending vehicle.

5. Learned Claims Tribunal framed the issues on the basis of pleadings of both the parties and after recording of evidence, allowed the claim petition filed by claimant and awarded compensation in favour of the claimant to the tune of Rs.2,46,200/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realisation.
6. Being aggrieved by impugned award, Insurance Company filed this appeal.
7. It is submitted on behalf of Insurance Company that learned Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding compensation in favour of claimant.
There was no accident occurred by an offending vehicle and the claim petition was filed by the claimant on the ground of false involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

He also submitted that owner and Driver filed their written statements before the Claims Tribunal in which, the owner has specifically pleaded that on the date of accident, he was present in the village Palduna along with alleged offending vehicle from NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35276 3 MA-2838-2023 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and the Claims Tribunal has ignored this aspect and also the certificate given by MPSEB (West), Naamli certifying the above fact.
Therefore, he prays for setting aside the impugned award.
8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant supported the impugned award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the entire record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found true that in written statement, the owner and Driver of the offending vehicle pleaded that on the date of accident, the owner of the offending vehicle was present in village Palduna along with alleged offending vehicle from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and with regard to this, the certificate given by the MPSEB (West), Naamli was certified the above facts.

But on perusal of the record, it is found that owner and Driver of the offending vehicle in their defence did not challenge before the witness box during trial to give evidence in support of pleadings.

10. It is well settled principle of law that the pleadings which are not supported by the evidence of the witnesses have no meaning and vice versa and the evidence which was not supported by the pleadings, has no meaning.
11.
In the present case, owner of the offending vehicle did not give any evidence in support of pleadings and was not duly proved by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, owner of the offending vehicle failed to prove that at the time of accident, he along with offending vehicle was present in village Palduna.

12. In view of the above discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, the claimant filed claim petition against the driver of the offending NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35276 4 MA-2838-2023 vehicle and police also registered case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Bherusingh Kalota on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145052022/

So, the Tribunal has rightly given a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle is involved in the alleged accident.
Accordingly, this appeal filed by the Insurance Company has no substance and the same is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
